record.paper_title: Supernomial Coefficients, Bailey's Lemma and Rogers-Ramanujan-Type Identities. A Survey of Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Let (q)_m = product_{i=1}^m (1 - q^i), (q)_infinity = product_{i=1}^infinity (1 - q^i), and let [a choose b]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. For the A2 Rogers-Ramanujan identity (q)_infinity sum_{r1,r2>=0} q^(r1^2 - r1 r2 + r2^2)/((q)_{r1}(q)_{r2}(q)_{r1+r2}) = sum_{r1,r2>=0} q^(r1^2 - r1 r2 + r2^2)/(q)_{r1} [2r1 choose r2]_q = product_{n>=0} 1/((1 - q^(7n+1))^2 (1 - q^(7n+3)) (1 - q^(7n+4)) (1 - q^(7n+6))^2), find a partition-theoretic interpretation for the middle sum. Preferably, first rewrite the left-hand side as a q-series that is both manifestly of A2 type and manifestly coefficientwise positive, and then give a combinatorial interpretation of that positive series.

evidence.quote: It seems a worthwhile exercise to find a partition theoretic interpretation for the middle term
manifestly of A2-type as well as manifestly positive

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Notation. For a non-negative integer $m$, set $(q)_m=\prod_{i=1}^m(1-q^i)$ with $(q)_0=1$, and let $(q)_\infty=\prod_{i=1}^\infty(1-q^i)$. For non-negative integers $a,b$, the Gaussian $q$-binomial coefficient is
$$\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{a}{b}_q=\begin{cases}\dfrac{(q)_a}{(q)_b\,(q)_{a-b}}&\text{if }0\le b\le a,\\[4pt]0&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}$$

Consider the $A_2$ Rogers–Ramanujan identity
$$(q)_\infty\sum_{r_1,r_2\ge 0}\frac{q^{r_1^2-r_1r_2+r_2^2}}{(q)_{r_1}(q)_{r_2}(q)_{r_1+r_2}}\;=\;\sum_{r_1,r_2\ge 0}\frac{q^{r_1^2-r_1r_2+r_2^2}}{(q)_{r_1}}\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{2r_1}{r_2}_q\;=\;\prod_{n\ge 0}\frac{1}{(1-q^{7n+1})^2(1-q^{7n+3})(1-q^{7n+4})(1-q^{7n+6})^2}.$$

Tasks:
(a) Express the left-hand side as a $q$-series that is simultaneously (i) manifestly of $A_2$ type (its summand reflects the $A_2$ root-system structure, e.g.\ involves the quadratic form $r_1^2-r_1r_2+r_2^2$ in an essential way) and (ii) manifestly coefficient-wise positive (each coefficient in the $q$-expansion is visibly a non-negative integer, with no need for cancellation).

(b) Give a partition-theoretic interpretation of the middle sum
$$\sum_{r_1,r_2\ge 0}\frac{q^{r_1^2-r_1r_2+r_2^2}}{(q)_{r_1}}\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{2r_1}{r_2}_q,$$
i.e.\ exhibit a class $\mathcal P$ of partitions (or coloured/multi-partitions) together with a statistic such that the generating function of $\mathcal P$ equals this sum, and such that $\mathcal P$ is naturally in bijection with the partitions enumerated by the infinite product on the right-hand side.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (e.g. Tsuchioka 2025 on $A_2^{(1)}$ level-3 bipartition identities, and Andrews–Schilling–Warnaar style $A_2$ Bailey-lemma developments) provides manifestly positive Andrews–Gordon-type series and some bipartition interpretations related to $A_2$ Rogers–Ramanujan identities. However, no source clearly establishes a partition-theoretic interpretation of the specific middle sum above in a way that is simultaneously manifestly of $A_2$ type and manifestly positive. The status appears unresolved in full generality.

status_evidence.title: An example of A_2 Rogers–Ramanujan bipartition identities of level 3
status_evidence.snippet: Manifestly positive Andrews–Gordon type series have been given for the level 3 standard modules of the affine Lie algebra of type A2(1), with corresponding bipartition identities.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on partition/bipartition interpretations of A_2 Rogers–Ramanujan identities exists, but at level 3 rather than the level-2 identity here.

status_evidence.title: Supernomial Coefficients, Bailey's Lemma and Rogers–Ramanujan-type Identities
status_evidence.snippet: It seems a worthwhile exercise to find a partition theoretic interpretation for the middle term ... manifestly of A2-type as well as manifestly positive.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly posed as an open exercise.
